title: Root Makefile to run backend and frontend dev servers
description: Add a root-level Makefile with targets to start the backend (FastAPI/uvicorn) and frontend (Vite) dev servers, individually and together, so contributors don't need to remember each service's own run command. Backend runs `backend/.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload` from the `backend/` directory (the venv is provisioned once by `.devcontainer/post-create.sh` inside the dev container); frontend runs `npm run dev` from the `frontend/` directory. Keep this a thin wrapper over existing tooling — no new build system, no reimplementing what `npm`/`uvicorn` already do.

checklist.step: Add a `make backend` target that runs `backend/.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload` from `backend/`, with a clear error message (not a raw path-not-found failure) if `backend/.venv` doesn't exist yet, pointing at `.devcontainer/post-create.sh` / `pip install -e ".[dev]"`.
Add a `make frontend` target that runs `npm run dev` from `frontend/`.

Add a combined target (e.g. `make dev`) that runs both concurrently and cleans up both processes on Ctrl-C/exit (e.g. background jobs plus a `trap ... EXIT` and `wait`) rather than leaving an orphaned process behind.

Decide whether to include adjacent convenience targets (e.g. `make install`, `make test`) or keep the Makefile scoped strictly to running the two dev servers as originally requested — record the call as a `decisions` entry either way.
Document the new `make` targets in README.md's existing run/setup instructions.
Verify each target actually works: start it, confirm the backend answers on its port and the frontend dev server serves the app, then stop cleanly with no leftover process.

decisions.decision: Added `make install` and `make test` as thin wrapper convenience targets alongside `backend`/`frontend`/`dev`, plus a self-documenting `make help` (also the `.DEFAULT_GOAL`). Did not add a `make lint` target.
decisions.rationale: `install` and `test` are exactly the two examples the checklist itself suggested, and each is a one-line passthrough to the same commands already documented in README.md (`pip install -e ".[dev]"`, `npm install`, `pytest`, `npm test`) — no new logic, so they don't violate the 'no new build system' framing in the task description. `make test` intentionally runs plain `pytest`/`vitest run` rather than the coverage-gated variants, since the dedicated `check-coverage`/`test-90` skills already own the 90% gate and duplicating that here would just create two sources of truth for the same check. Skipped a `lint`/static-analysis target for the same reason: the `static-verify` skill already owns running ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc together with its own reporting conventions (grouping findings, distinguishing type errors from style nits) that a bare Makefile passthrough would flatten. `help` was added because a Makefile with six targets is easy to forget the names of; it's a standard `grep`-the-`## comment` pattern, not a build-system addition. Rejected alternative: keeping the Makefile to only `backend`/`frontend`/`dev` (strict scope) — rejected as under-serving the checklist's explicit prompt to decide on `install`/`test`. Also rejected: a `lint` target mirroring `static-verify` — rejected as duplicating an existing skill's job.

decisions.decision: `make dev`'s cleanup traps and kills the two `$(MAKE) backend`/`$(MAKE) frontend` child PIDs it captured itself (`kill $$bpid $$fpid`), not the whole process group (`kill 0`).
decisions.rationale: An initial `trap 'kill 0' EXIT INT TERM` implementation was verified to actually clean up both uvicorn and vite with no orphaned processes, but under a live SIGINT it also signalled the trapping shell itself mid-handler and reproducibly crashed bash in this environment (reported by make as 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)' on the `dev` recipe) — alarming output for something that otherwise worked correctly. Switching to killing only the two captured child PIDs produces the same clean-shutdown outcome (verified: `INFO: Shutting down` / `Application shutdown complete` from uvicorn, vite's process group gone, `pgrep -fa 'uvicorn|vite'` empty afterward) with a normal 'Interrupt' exit instead of a spurious crash report. Rejected alternative: keep `kill 0` since it's the more commonly cited idiom for this pattern — rejected once the self-signal crash was reproduced twice under a real SIGINT to the process group (the realistic Ctrl-C scenario), not just under `timeout`.

decisions.decision: Fixed the SIGTERM-orphan blocker (pr-reviewer's reversal comment) two ways together: (1) `make backend`/`make frontend` are now launched with `setsid $(MAKE) backend </dev/null` / `setsid $(MAKE) frontend </dev/null` instead of a bare `$(MAKE) ... &`, so each sub-make becomes the leader of its own new session/process group whose pgid equals the pid captured by `$!` — the cleanup trap then does `kill -TERM -$$bpid -$$fpid`, a *negative*-pid (process-group) kill that reaches uvicorn's forked `--reload` watcher and npm's forked vite/node process, not just the immediate sub-make. (2) Removed the `dev` recipe's outer `( ... )` subshell grouping. Root-caused via direct reproduction: with the parens present, make's recipe shell (make's own direct child, which is what GNU Make's fatal-signal handler actually forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM to) is only the *outer* `sh -c '(...)'` process; the `(...)` group itself forks a *second*, nested subshell to hold the background jobs/trap/wait, and that nested subshell is never in make's direct child relationship, so it never receives the forwarded signal at all — confirmed by reproducing the exact orphaning pr-reviewer reported, then tracing which pid a plain `kill -TERM <top-make-pid>` actually reached (only the outer wrapper shell, which has no trap and dies immediately on default disposition, orphaning the inner subshell and everything under it). Removing the parens means the recipe's multi-line, backslash-continued command is already passed to the shell as a single `sh -c` invocation with no extra grouping needed, so the trap now lives on make's actual direct child and gets the forwarded signal.
decisions.rationale: Verified end-to-end after the fix, from a separate shell against a backgrounded `make dev`: (a) plain `kill -TERM <top-pid>` (the reported failure mode — systemd ExecStop/supervisor-default/Docker-PID1/bare `kill`) now yields uvicorn's `Shutting down`/`Application shutdown complete`/`Stopping reloader process` and vite's process exiting, `ss -ltnp` shows :8000/:5173 free, `pgrep -fa 'uvicorn|vite'` empty; (b) interactive-terminal-style Ctrl-C (`setsid`+`kill -INT` on the whole negative PGID) still cleans up the same way with no bash crash (the earlier `kill 0` segfault was specifically from the trapping shell signalling its own process group including itself — targeting the two child groups' pgids explicitly, never PGID 0, avoids that self-signal case entirely; both signals tested, not just one). Rejected alternatives: (i) keep `$(MAKE) ... &` (no `setsid`) and instead have the trap `pkill -P` recursively down each sub-make's descendant tree — rejected as needing a manual tree walk to reach uvicorn's/vite's non-exec'd forked descendants, more fragile than one `setsid`+negative-pid kill per branch; (ii) `pkill -f` scoped to the literal uvicorn/vite command strings — rejected as brittle to argument-string drift (e.g. an added uvicorn flag) and riskier of false-positive matches on an unrelated process; (iii) leave the `( ... )` parens in place and instead try to propagate the trap through an extra layer (e.g. re-trapping inside the nested subshell some other way) — rejected once it was clear the parens were the root cause of the signal never reaching the trap-holding process at all, not just an incidental detail; removing them is strictly simpler and was verified to have no other effect on the recipe's behavior (still one shell invocation, same background/trap/wait semantics). Also verified the non-blocking SIGINT-to-top-pid-only hang (dev-makefile-followups item 1) still reproduces after this fix and is unrelated to it: GNU Make itself explicitly ignores SIGINT while a recipe's child is executing (by design, deferring interactive Ctrl-C delivery to the terminal's whole-foreground-process-group semantics), so a bare SIGINT to only the top pid never even reaches the recipe shell to forward — this is inherent to GNU Make and out of reach of any trap written inside the recipe, so left as documented, non-blocking, and not attempted here per the task's 'fix only if it doesn't complicate the main fix' guidance. Also updated README.md's wording (dev-makefile-followups item 2) since it was a one-line, low-risk fix alongside this: `make dev` invoking `make backend` as a subprocess of its own recipe is no longer described as a formal Make prerequisite ('depends on').

comments.summary: RESOLVED (round 2): the round-1 blocking finding -- `make dev`'s cleanup trap only killed the two immediate `$(MAKE) backend`/`$(MAKE) frontend` PIDs, not the uvicorn/vite processes further down the tree, so a plain `kill <top-pid>` (SIGTERM) orphaned them -- is fixed. task-worker now launches each sub-make via `setsid $(MAKE) backend </dev/null` / `setsid $(MAKE) frontend </dev/null` (each becomes leader of its own process group) and the trap does `kill -TERM -$$bpid -$$fpid` (negative pid = whole process group), and removed the recipe's outer `( ... )` subshell grouping so the trap sits on the shell make's fatal-signal handler actually forwards to. Independently re-verified myself (not just reading the report): read the current Makefile directly to confirm the mechanism is present, then reproduced `kill -TERM <top-level make dev pid>` from a separate shell against a live backgrounded run -- uvicorn shuts down cleanly (Shutting down / Application shutdown complete / Stopping reloader process), vite/node exits, ports 8000/5173 free, `pgrep -fa 'uvicorn|vite'` empty. Also re-verified interactive-Ctrl-C-style (setsid + kill -INT on the negative PGID) still works with no bash crash. Ran this cleanup end-to-end successfully across multiple separate repro runs.

Non-blocking (new, found via a backgrounded code-review pass I independently reproduced myself before recording): `make dev`'s `wait $$bpid $$fpid` only returns once *both* sub-targets have exited, so if one fails immediately (e.g. `backend/.venv` missing) the other (e.g. frontend/vite) keeps running indefinitely instead of `make dev` exiting/reporting overall failure -- an easy-to-miss partial failure in scrolling/non-interactive output. Reproduced directly with `backend/.venv` temporarily moved aside: backend's clear venv-missing error prints and that sub-make exits with Error 1, but vite starts right after and `make dev` itself never exits on its own; had to be interrupted manually. Distinct from the round-1 orphan bug: the surviving process is still attached to the trap and cleans up correctly once you do stop it (verified: no leftover process afterward) -- this is a fail-fast/UX gap, not a leak, so non-blocking. Filed as a new checklist item on docs/tasks/dev-makefile-followups.json.

Non-blocking, already resolved in this round: README's "make backend (and make dev, which depends on it)" wording was fixed to describe `dev` invoking `$(MAKE) backend` as a subprocess of its own recipe rather than a formal Make prerequisite -- confirmed in the current README.md diff. Corresponding dev-makefile-followups checklist item already marked done.

review.notes: Retry round 2 of 3. Read the current Makefile myself (did not trust task-worker's report) and independently reproduced the exact SIGTERM-to-top-level-pid scenario that blocked round 1 -- confirmed fixed, no orphans, across multiple separate repro runs (a `timeout`-command-mediated run once left a stray vite process, but a direct `kill -TERM` to the same backgrounded top pid cleaned up correctly on retry and on a second `timeout`-based retry, so this reads as a `timeout`-harness artifact from my own test setup, not a reproducible defect in the Makefile's own signal handling -- not filed as a finding). Also independently reproduced and confirmed the interactive-Ctrl-C-style case still works with no bash crash. Backend: pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90 -> 493 passed, 99.84% coverage, no regression. Frontend: vitest run --coverage -> 99.71%/99.64%/100%/99.71%, no regression. Static analysis: ruff, mypy, eslint, tsc all clean. No API/OpenAPI change, no new module/dependency/layer (architecture-review n/a), no signal/portfolio code (verify-elder-signal n/a, area is infra), no frontend components touched (browser walkthrough explicitly n/a -- Makefile + docs only). Checklist item 4 ("decide whether to include adjacent convenience targets") has a matching decisions entry -- no gap. No human PR comments found overriding automation. One new non-blocking finding (dev target doesn't fail-fast when one sub-target dies early) filed to docs/tasks/dev-makefile-followups.json rather than blocking; it was found via a backgrounded code-review pass that finished after my accept was already posted, but I independently reproduced it myself before recording it as a finding (per the lesson from this PR's own round-1 review: don't take an automated pass on faith, verify directly) -- unlike round 1's reversal, this finding doesn't contradict or invalidate the accept, so posted as an addendum PR comment rather than a verdict reversal. Verdict: accepted.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend suite (pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing): 493 passed, 99.84% coverage, matches review notes. Read the Makefile diff myself and confirmed it matches the review's described setsid/negative-pid-kill/no-outer-subshell mechanism. Directly reproduced the key claim from a separate shell: backgrounded `make dev`, verified process tree (backend pgid, frontend pgid distinct via setsid), sent plain `kill -TERM` to the top-level make dev pid, confirmed uvicorn's clean shutdown log (Shutting down / Application shutdown complete / Stopping reloader process), ports 8000/5173 freed, and `pgrep -fa 'uvicorn|vite'` empty afterward -- no orphans. Also checked PR #96 comments: all from the shared automation account, no human override. dev-makefile-followups.json exists with correct index.json mirroring for the filed non-blocking finding.
